bullets.text: Halvern Dam on the Sorrel River above Brindlemark in the Assek Valley was reported damaged on 9 September 2025, together with its right abutment.
The dam safety alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange the following morning and a mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow.
Roughly 11,800 residents were evacuated from Brindlemark in the first phase, with a later figure of 12,400 given, and displaced people moved on to Quennard.
Police deployed to Brindlemark, assistance was provided in Quennard and the Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the dam's condition.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment are reported damaged on the afternoon of the first day.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provides information on the dam damage.
The next morning a mandatory evacuation is ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow and the alert level is raised from Yellow to Orange; roughly 11,800 residents leave Brindlemark.
By evening the evacuated figure is given as 12,400, displaced people move away from Quennard, assistance is provided in Quennard and police deploy to Brindlemark.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment were damaged.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow as the dam alert escalated.
Roughly 11,800 residents were evacuated from Brindlemark, with further residents moved from Ferris Hollow.
The evacuated figure rose to 12,400 by the evening of the second day.
People were displaced from Quennard, moving away from the city as the emergency continued.
Police deployed to Brindlemark during the evacuation.
The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange as the evacuation was ordered.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the damage to the dam.
Assistance was provided to displaced people in Quennard.
